deck_title: Cayley rational SO(3) Lie rotor vs naive Forward Euler cross-product volume inflation rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Arthur Cayley (1846) rational SO(3) Lie-algebra transform (R_Cayley = (I + A)(I - A)^(-1) = I + (2 / (1 + a·a))([a]_x + [a]_x^2) with a = 0.5 * omega * dt, requiring zero sin/cos/sqrt calls and locking volume determinant det(R_Cayley) = (1 + ||a||^2)/(1 + ||a||^2) = 1.0000x across all 17 angular-step stations u = ||omega*dt||^2 in [0.0000, 1.0000] with 0/17 inflated stations) versus naive first-order Forward Euler cross-product update (v_next = v + (omega*dt) x v, whose matrix R_Euler = I + [omega*dt]_x inflates radial norm squared and volume determinant as det(I + [omega*dt]_x) = 1 + u to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x / +100% double volume at u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-substep SO(3) Lie exponential map.
